create.name: Barre Center for Buddhist Studies
create.bio:
The Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (BCBS) is a non-profit centre for Buddhist study and practice in the country town of Barre, in central Massachusetts. Joseph Goldstein and Sharon Salzberg started it in 1990 so that the study of Buddhist texts and meditation could be explored together. It draws mainly on early Buddhism but is not tied to one school, and its visiting faculty come from Theravada, Chan and Zen, Tibetan and secular backgrounds, among them Guo Gu, Kaira Jewel Lingo, Lama Rod Owens, Joan Halifax, Shaila Catherine and Akincano Weber.

Programs run from a weekend to more than a year. On the Barre campus, a farmhouse among woods and fields, there are residential courses that combine teaching sessions with silent sitting, alongside hybrid retreats that can also be joined online. Online, BCBS offers cohort programmes over several weeks, such as a nine-week study of the Satipatthana Sutta built on Bhikkhu Analayo's teaching, and a free weekday lunchtime sitting with a talk on Zoom. Prices are set on a sliding scale with financial assistance, some programmes are offered for dana, and recorded talks, a journal and a bookshop are on its website.

courses.title: Gateway to Chan Hybrid Retreat
courses.description: A Chan retreat with Guo Gu, joined at Barre or online, built around half-hour sitting periods alternated with mindful yoga and walking meditation.
courses.price: Online Prices Benefactor: $299 Actual Cost: $249 Partially Supported: $219 Supported: $189 Residential Prices Benefactor: $1495 Actual Cost: $1095 Partially Supported: $895 Supported: $695 Commuter: $425

courses.title: In the Buddha's Presence: Individuality and Liberation
courses.description: A four-night residential course with Akincano Weber that reads the Dharma through the lives of people who met the Buddha, and how their different natures shaped their paths.
courses.price: Residential Prices Benefactor: $1200 Actual Cost: $800 Supported: $560 Commuter: $380

courses.title: Seeing That Frees: Exploring the Path of Emptiness
courses.description: A five-night residential retreat, with Yahel Avigur among its teachers, working step by step with the emptiness practices set out in Rob Burbea's book of the same name.
courses.price: Residential Prices Benefactor: $1500 Actual Cost: $1000 Supported: $700 Commuter: $475

courses.title: Satipaṭṭhāna Meditation
courses.description: A nine-week online cohort programme of study and practice with the Satipatthana Sutta, guided by Bhikkhu Analayo's teachings, at seven to ten hours a week. Applications close on 1 February 2027.

free_resources.title: The Daily Sit
free_resources.description: A free 45-minute Zoom session every weekday at noon US Eastern time, hosted by Bill and Susan Morgan: talks with guided meditation on some days, questions or a silent sit on others.

free_resources.title: Practicing Jhānas & Emptiness: Surprising Similarities, Distinctive Differences
free_resources.description: An online conversation between Leigh Brasington and Heather Sundberg on how absorption practice and emptiness practice meet and part, offered freely on a dana basis with a recording afterwards.

free_resources.title: Dharma Recordings
free_resources.description: Recorded talks and teachings from BCBS programmes, free to stream.
